"""Post one fake invoice to the ledger sandbox and print the reference."""
import os
import sys


def main():
    token = os.environ.get("LEDGER_SANDBOX_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        print(
            "error: LEDGER_SANDBOX_TOKEN is not set. Sandbox tokens expire after 7 days; "
            "mint a new one with `acmectl tokens mint ledger-sbx` and export it.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1
    print("posting a test invoice to the ledger sandbox")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```
error: LEDGER_SANDBOX_TOKEN is not set. Sandbox tokens expire after 7 days; mint a new one with `acmectl tokens mint ledger-sbx` and export it.
```

To get past this, mint a token and run the script again:

```bash
export LEDGER_SANDBOX_TOKEN=$(acmectl tokens mint ledger-sbx)   # or paste the minted token
python scripts/ledger_smoke.py
```

I didn't mint the token myself because it creates a credential under your account. I can do it and re-run the test if you want.

Even with a token, the script as written only checks that the variable is set and prints "posting a test invoice to the ledger sandbox". It doesn't send any request or print a reference, despite what its docstring says. So a pass right now wouldn't prove the sandbox works. If you want a real end-to-end check, the script needs the actual POST added.
